summary: This diff is purely additive infrastructure (new YAML doc, a MASTER_INDEX registry entry, and two new Node.js scripts) with no changes to migrations/schema/auth/payment/permission/rls paths and no touches to .github/workflows/**, so tier1 classification is correct; the code itself is internally consistent (persistent-profile.js's CHROME_EXECUTABLE path and LD_LIBRARY_PATH composition match the documented dpkg-deb -x extraction layout and the CLI launcher wrapper, the repo has no root package.json so CommonJS require() is safe, and smoketest.js correctly closes the browser context in a finally block and exits non-zero on failure with a captured stack), no secrets or credentials are committed (the VNC password is generated at runtime, and the task explicitly and correctly refrains from ever automating the actual Google login, deferring that one step to a documented manual human procedure), and the security posture for the always-on pieces is reasonable (profile dir locked to 700 rajat-only, VNC bound to loopback only and reachable solely via SSH tunnel with a per-session random password, torn down immediately after use). Two non-blocking concerns worth tracking as follow-ups rather than reasons to reject: (1) both scripts hardcode absolute /opt/veridian/... paths with no environment-variable override, so they are tied to this specific server's directory layout and will silently break if that layout changes; (2) --no-sandbox is used for Chrome (justified by precedent and the single-trusted-user host model, but still a real reduction in browser process isolation that matters more once this profile holds a live Google session and navigates to arbitrary sites) and the one-time VNC login path relies on a hacky ELF string-patch of xkbcomp staged into /tmp, which is scoped to a torn-down-after-use session but is an unusual technique worth another look if VNC usage expands beyond this single login event.
issues: Hardcoded absolute /opt/veridian/... paths in scripts/browser/persistent-profile.js with no override mechanism, making the helper non-portable across environments

--no-sandbox Chrome flag reduces process-level isolation; acceptable for now per documented single-user host rationale but should be revisited once the profile holds a real authenticated Google session and may navigate untrusted sites

VNC one-time-login workaround patches a hardcoded path inside the xkbcomp ELF binary and stages a binary in /tmp; scoped and torn down after use, but worth revisiting if this VNC path sees more than the single documented login event
